title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building an explicit, rigid model of the closed annulus X = U × I, with U the unit circle and I = [-1,1]. The model carries a large group of 'affine' symmetries. Its purpose is to isolate the Dehn twist along a cylinder as a concrete group element, as a building block for his Teichmüller 'Lego' (gluing surfaces along cylinders).

On the previous page he lets D_R = {1,σ} ⋉ R act on the universal cover R̃_ε of each boundary circle U_ε, ε = ±1: R acts by translation and σ by t ↦ -t. This action descends to D_U on U_ε. The product D_R × D_R acts on the cover of ∂X. He then restricts to the subgroup D_{R×R} = {1,σ} ⋉ (R×R), in which a single σ acts on both factors. The aim is to extend the action to the universal cover X̃ = R × I → X, (t,s) ↦ (exp 2iπt, s).

This page:
(1) For u = (u_{-1},u_1) ∈ R×R, let s ↦ u_s be the affine interpolation, u_s = ((u_1 - u_{-1})/2) s + (u_1 + u_{-1})/2. The handwritten 'R^*×R' is evidently R×R.
(2) The action on X̃ is given by u·(t,s) = (t + u_s, s) and σ·(t,s) = (-t, s). The relation σuσ^{-1} = -u holds, so this is a genuine action of the semidirect product. It is fibred over the projection X̃ → I, with the trivial action on I.
(3) The action commutes with the deck group Z (t ↦ t+1), since it is affine in t with slope ±1. It therefore descends to an action on X = U × I, again fibred over I.
(4) The subgroup acting trivially on ∂X = U × {±1} is Z×Z, i.e. u_{-1}, u_1 ∈ Z. It lies in the identity component D̊ = R×R.

The next page completes the picture. D_{R×R} acts faithfully on X̃. Two elements act identically on X iff ν = ν', u_1 - u_{-1} = u'_1 - u'_{-1}, and (u_1+u_{-1})/2 ≡ (u'_1+u'_{-1})/2 mod Z. So the kernel on X is the diagonal Z. The image of Z×Z in Homeo(X, rel ∂X) is Z×Z/ΔZ ≅ Z, generated by u = (0,1), i.e. (t,s) ↦ (t + (s+1)/2, s). This is the standard Dehn twist.

The continuous part R×R/ΔZ gives a 'twist flow'. It is the topological analogue of the Fenchel–Nielsen twist parameter, plus independent rotations of the two boundary circles. σ is the orientation-reversing reflection preserving each boundary component. The problem served is to describe, functorially and with explicit coordinates (a,b), the group of affine automorphisms of a cylinder and its relation to the Dehn twist and to boundary rotations, for use in gluing.
errors: The handwritten '(u_{-1},u_1) ∈ ℝ*×ℝ' (transcribed as R^*×R) must be ℝ×ℝ. The mark is a smudge or correction; a nonzero condition plays no role.
Minor: the claim that the subgroup acting trivially on ∂X is Z×Z is correct. The page does not yet note that its diagonal acts trivially on all of X; this is done on the next page via (17)–(20).
Minor: the indexing is written in two styles, (u_1, u_1)/(u_{-1}, u_1) and u_{+1}/u_1. These are notational slips only.

ideas.what: Affine 'shear' action of R×R on the strip R×I by interpolating boundary translations, descending to the annulus.
ideas.modern_name: Explicit model of twist maps on a cylinder; Dehn twist as a linear shear (t,s) ↦ (t + (s+1)/2, s).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dehn (1938), Lickorish (1960s); a standard textbook construction.
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts. The Esquisse d'un programme mentions Teichmüller groupoids and cylinders but not this model.

ideas.what: Group D_{R×R} = {1,σ} ⋉ (R×R) of boundary-rotation pairs plus a reflection, acting on the annulus. The subgroup trivial on the boundary is Z×Z, and the kernel on X is the diagonal Z.
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group of the annulus rel boundary ≅ Z (Dehn twist); boundary rotations / framed boundary; twist flow (cf. Fenchel–Nielsen twist).
ideas.where_published: Unsure whether any circulated Teichmüller notes contain this.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard explicit construction of the Dehn twist and the boundary-rotation group of an annulus. It is a preparatory bookkeeping step in the Teichmüller notes, with no new result or unusual connection.
transcription_corrections: '(u_{-1},u_1)∈ℝ^*×ℝ' should read ℝ×ℝ; the mark over the first ℝ is a correction or smudge.
In (15) the handwriting has '(u_1,u_1).(t,s)', which is intended as (u_{-1},u_1); the transcription's (u_{-1},u_1) is correct.
'{+plus commodément+}' is on the previous page; on this page 'ℝ dans ℝ [-def-] qui' should read 'qui,' with 'def' struck out.
